newsitem.title: UK: Regulator, Brit Gas agree price controls.
newsitem.headline: Regulator, Brit Gas agree price controls.

text.p: British Gas said on Friday it reached agreement with industry regulator Ofgas on new price controls which will see average domestic gas bills in Britain drop by about seven pounds ($11) in 1997/1998.
Both parties, which are fighting over price caps for British Gas' separate pipeline transport business, were widely expected to reach agreement on domestic gas prices.

"When the initial proposals were put forward in June we had a number of serious concerns. Although we still believe the proposals are tough, we expect to accept them as long as they are unchanged following the statutory consultation period," said British Gas' deputy chairman Philip Rogerson in a statement.

The agreement covers the company's pricing in the domestic market of some 18 million customers, which is scheduled to be opened up to nationwide competition from other gas suppliers by the end of 1998.
A pilot project in the south west of England started in April, while competition is set to be expanded to the south east early in 1997.
Ofgas said the new controls mean customers' bills will be cut by about four percent a year for three years on top of the initial seven pound cut.
